Needs changes before merge. This is a safety-tier review.

The new draft and refusal pins pass. Both chamfer integration suites also pass.

**Requested before merge**

1. **Keep the refusal for a bevel that ends below half depth.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs:223`.
   A bevel can pass this test without being one straight drafted wall. Use a bevel with a width of 0.25 mm and a depth of 0.7 mm. The wall below it is vertical. For a ride depth of 1 mm, its top, middle and corner offsets are 0.25, 0.071428571 and 0 mm.
   The test reads `d = 0.25` and `dm = 0.178571`. Its residual is 0.053571, below the permitted 0.0625. The PR accepts the loop as drafted. It returns both the outer wall and the sharp pocket. The earlier code refuses the same top and corner sections. Thus the operation can cut edges that the model leaves sharp.
   The isolated regression fails with the PR module and passes with the upstream module. Use a check that proves a straight wall, or refuse these sections. Add a regression with the existing helper:

   ```rust
   let (top, mid, corner) = x0_side_off(0.25, 0.25 * (0.7 - 0.5) / 0.7);
   assert!(ride_loops(&top, &mid, &corner, 1.0, 1.0, 9.0, UPRIGHT).is_err());
   ```

2. **Run the reached heavy lanes on the final head.** Upstream [AGENTS.md:632](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba/AGENTS.md#L632) and the PR body, `Not exercised`.
   The heavy plan reaches every motion and app heavy target. The PR body says that these lanes did not run. Current upstream law blocks readiness until those tests pass. Run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head. Add the lane results to the body. I did not run the heavy or light lanes. They are not passes.

**Local build and tests**

The worktree was `.claude/worktrees/review-3126`. I trial-merged the PR with main at `6b63e442bc0705707b1a300bc96faf5aadcf21bd`. The trial merge was clean. All builds and tests ran locally.

- `RUSTC_WRAPPER= CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 140 steps, 0 failed. The test totals are 1952 passed, 0 failed and 64 ignored.
- The quick gate built the selected motion and app targets with `--no-run`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed, with the compile cache disabled.
- `chamfer_modelled_edge`: 7 passed. `chamfer_partly_bevelled`: 2 passed.
- The first planner build stalled in sccache. The retry disabled the cache.
- Goldens moved: none.

**Extra suites run**

No test data or importer file changed. The extra fixture and importer suites do not apply.

An external Cargo harness used copies of the chamfer module and the built motion library. It did not edit the repository source.

- The PR module's existing chamfer ride tests: 16 passed.
- `review_a_bevel_ending_below_mid_depth_must_still_refuse`: failed with the PR module; passed with the upstream module.


- Removed the half-depth check in a temporary copy: `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft` failed. The unchanged copy passes.
- Removed the slope limit in a temporary copy: `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer` failed. The unchanged copy passes.

Needs changes before merge. This is a safety-tier review.

The new short-bevel regression passes. The quick gate, clippy, and both light tests also pass.
The earlier short-bevel finding is met. The body now records a full heavy run on this head.

**Requested before merge**

1. **Refuse a wall whose slope reverses at half depth.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs:220-223`.
   The test uses unsigned distances. It does not prove that the middle section lies between the top and corner sections.
   Use the existing helper with `x0_side_off(0.2, 0.3)` and a ride depth of 1 mm.
   At Z10, Z9.5, and Z9, the side stands at X0.2, X0.3, and X0.
   This side bends back at half depth. It is not one straight drafted wall.
   However, `d = 0.2` and `dm = 0.1`, so the residual is zero.
   The PR accepts this loop as drafted. It returns the outer wall and the sharp pocket.
   Thus the chamfer can select edges that the model leaves sharp, instead of refusing the partial bevel.
   The same top and corner sections refuse with the current upstream module.
   Check the direction and correspondence of the sections. Refuse a reversed slope and add this regression:

   ```rust
   let (top, mid, corner) = x0_side_off(0.2, 0.3);
   assert!(ride_loops(&top, &mid, &corner, 1.0, 1.0, 9.0, UPRIGHT).is_err());
   ```

   I ran this check in an external Cargo harness. It fails with the PR module and passes with the upstream module.
   The PR result is `Ok(Region)` with two loops, including the pocket at X20..40, Y15..25.
   No repository source was changed.

   ```text
   a reversed slope must refuse, got Ok(Region { loops: [Loop { pts: [Point2 { x: 60.0, y: 40.0 }, Point2 { x: 0.0, y: 40.0 }, Point2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }, Point2 { x: 60.0, y: 0.0 }] }, Loop { pts: [Point2 { x: 20.0, y: 25.0 }, Point2 { x: 40.0, y: 25.0 }, Point2 { x: 40.0, y: 15.0 }, Point2 { x: 20.0, y: 15.0 }] }] })
   ```

**Local build and tests**

I trial-merged this head with upstream main at `9744a9acfe0ae6f9e9089f9ec317571cca643dfd`.
The merge was clean. All review commands ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3126`.
No GitHub runner was used. The compile cache was disabled.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 144 steps passed in 33.5 minutes. Tests: 1987 passed, 0 failed, 66 ignored.
- The quick gate built the selected motion and app targets with `--no-run`.
- Motion library: 507 passed, 10 ignored. App library: 297 passed.
- `chamfer_modelled_edge`: 7 passed. `chamfer_partly_bevelled`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: all 3 steps passed. Both light tests passed.
- The isolated unchanged chamfer module: all 17 existing tests passed.
- Goldens moved: none. UI screenshots do not apply. No UI file changed.

**Extra suites run**

No fixture, golden, test data, or importer file changed. The extra fixture and importer suites do not apply.
The isolated reversed-slope check is the additional regression described above.

**Mutations**

Each mutation used a separate copy under `/tmp`. The unchanged copy passed each named pin.

- Half-depth check removed: `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft` failed; unchanged check passed.
- Slope limit removed: `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer` failed; unchanged check passed.
- Former 25% slack restored: `a_bevel_ending_below_half_depth_is_no_draft` failed; `LEAN_SLACK` passed.

**Heavy lanes**

The dry plan reaches every motion and app heavy target.
I rely on the author's recorded full run on `5e745b74430e4186f3bf293a23aa8b462a217fba` for those lanes:
235 steps passed, 100 tests passed, and six known-fail validations failed as expected.
The author records 57 motion tests and 43 app tests.
Current main adds two app targets to the plan: `first_traverse_posed` and `mcp_edit_machine`.
Their entry files have no ignored tests. Their helper modules select them conservatively.
I also ran `motion heavy: adaptive_troch_parallel` locally on the trial merge. Both its ignored tests passed.

**Notes**

No new command, dependency, process file, snapshot PNG, or golden is changed.
The decision file records the draft rule and the tighter slack.
The reversed-slope result above still blocks readiness.
